sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Millville, NJ?
sections.html:
Millville is a Cumberland County city where the main local rule for a seller concerns tenants. Roughly 36 percent of occupied homes are rented, so many sales involve a registered rental unit, and the city's registration and inspection code shapes what a buyer inherits.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate puts Millville at 28,098 residents, and its 2020 to 2024 survey counts 11,845 households averaging 2.30 people. Owner occupancy is 64.1 percent, the median owner value is $219,000, and median gross rent is $1,261. Median household income is $70,275, and 20.2 percent of residents are 65 or older. With a median value that low, comparable Cumberland County sales matter more to your price than any statewide average.

sections.h2: How did Millville grow into the city it is today?
sections.html:
Millville was incorporated as a township on February 24, 1801, from part of Fairfield Township, and became a city on March 1, 1866 after a referendum. The name comes from a proposal for a mill town on the Maurice River. Sawmills came first, then in 1806 an Irish immigrant opened the first glass factory, drawing on local silica sand and wood. Millville roses, a style of paperweight, take their name from the city.

The city covers 44.50 square miles, 42.00 of them land, and borders Commercial, Deerfield, Downe, Fairfield, Lawrence and Maurice River townships plus Vineland. Clarks Mill, Farmingdale, Manatico, North Newark and Union Lake are named places inside the city lines. In 1936 the city opened Roosevelt Park, the country's first retirement colony for older residents, on land it had repossessed for back taxes. Millville Army Air Field opened in January 1943 as a gunnery school and later returned to the city as Millville Airport.

sections.h2: What happens when a Millville house has tenants?
sections.html:
Chapter 11, Article VII of the Millville code requires every residential rental unit, single family homes included, to be registered and inspected each year and again with each change in occupancy. No one may live in an unregistered unit. After a satisfactory inspection the city issues a certificate of continued occupancy, and none is issued while violations remain open.

Millville rental registration and inspection charges
ItemCharge or rule
Annual registration and inspection$100 per unit
Paid after the due date$125 per unit
Added inspection, reinspection or cancellation with under 48 hours' notice$50 each
Registration termsAbout 25 percent of units start on each of January 1, April 1, July 1 and October 1
Exempt unitsUnits owned by the city, the Millville Housing Authority or another government agency

Source: City of Millville Code, Chapter 11, Article VII, Residential Rental Properties.

An owner who lives outside Cumberland County must name an agent who lives or works in the county. The lease must say it is subject to city ordinances, and at a change of occupancy the owner hands over the state Truth in Renting guide. If you are selling a tenant-occupied house, ask the Bureau of Permits and Inspections for the registration status before you list.

sections.h2: Does a Millville sale need a city inspection?
sections.html:
Millville's code spells out inspections for rental units, and it does not describe a separate sale certificate for an owner-occupied house. Ask the Bureau of Permits and Inspections whether a change of ownership triggers a certificate of continued occupancy or any other inspection for an owner-occupied house, and request the permit history for the address.

  • Ask whether any open permit still needs a final inspection before closing.
  • If tenants stay in place, the rental certificate and the annual inspection carry forward to the new owner.

sections.h2: How do roads, jobs and local attractions compare in Millville?
sections.html:
Workers in Millville average 25.2 minutes getting to their jobs, by the Census count. The city sits between the southern ends of the New Jersey Turnpike, the Garden State Parkway, Route 55 and the Atlantic City Expressway.

  • Roads: Routes 47, 49 and 55 cross the city, and 172.73 miles of roadway are split among the city, Cumberland County and the state.
  • Transit: NJ Transit bus routes 313 from Cape May to Philadelphia, 408 between Millville and Philadelphia, and 553 toward Atlantic City.
  • Air: Millville Airport, run by the Delaware River and Bay Authority, serves general aviation.
  • Culture and recreation: the Glasstown Arts District, Wheaton Arts, the Levoy Theatre (reopened September 2012), New Jersey Motorsports Park and Laurel Lake.

Rowan College of South Jersey, Cumberland Campus, sits partly inside the city limits.

sections.h2: How do Millville schools and weather affect a listing?
sections.html:
Millville Public Schools run nine schools with 5,107 students in 2021-22, among them Lakeside Middle School and Millville Senior High School with 1,638 students. The district is one of the state's former Abbott districts, which means the Schools Development Authority covers its building projects. A $137 million expansion that began in 2019 adds 82,000 square feet at the high school so every high schooler can attend in one building. Commercial, Lawrence and Maurice River townships send their high school students here, and the Cumberland County Technical Education Center in Millville is tuition free for county residents.

The climate is humid subtropical, with 43.37 inches of precipitation in an average year. January lows average near 24 degrees, the record high is 103 and the record low is minus 10. Roofs, gutters and crawlspace drainage get the closest look in an inspection after a wet stretch.

sections.h2: How do Millville taxes, appeals and the transfer fee work?
sections.html:
The Millville Tax Collector bills on a calendar year, mails bills in mid to late July, and each bill has four stubs for August, November, February and May. The city allows a 10-day grace period, and the collector cannot honor postmarks, so a payment must arrive by the 10th. Interest is 8 percent on the first $1,500 of delinquency and 18 percent above that, with a 6 percent year-end penalty on balances over $10,000 left on June 30. Charges unpaid on the 11th day of the 11th month are delinquent and subject to the annual tax sale.

Cumberland County's Board of Taxation takes regular appeals from the first business day of January through April 1 at 4:00 PM, with no exceptions for lateness. In a town revalued for the current year the window runs to May 1, and added or omitted assessments can be appealed from October 1 through December 1.

The seller also owes the state's Realty Transfer Fee at recording. At the Census median of $219,000, the state's rates for sales up to $350,000 work out to $1,083.20: $600 on the first $150,000, $335 on the next $50,000 and $148.20 on the remaining $19,000.

sections.h2: Where does a Millville deed get recorded?
sections.html: A Millville deed is recorded with the Cumberland County Clerk, which keeps an office in Bridgeton and another at the Cumberland Mall. Ask the clerk's office for the current recording fee and cover sheet requirements before closing day, and ask your closing agent who files the deed and settles the transfer fee.

faqs.q: What does Millville charge to register a rental house?
faqs.a: Millville charges $100 per unit each year, rising to $125 when paid late. A single family house that is rented counts as a unit, and added inspections or short-notice cancellations cost $50 each.

faqs.q: When is the Cumberland County appeal deadline for a Millville assessment?
faqs.a: The regular deadline is April 1 at 4:00 PM, and the county says there are no exceptions for lateness. When April 1 falls on a weekend the deadline moves to the next business day, and a municipality revalued that year gets until May 1.

faqs.q: When do Millville property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Bills are due on August, November, February and May stubs with a 10-day grace period. Charges still owed on the 11th day of the 11th month are treated as delinquent and can go to the city's annual tax sale.

faqs.q: Do tenants have to move out before a Millville sale?
faqs.a: Nothing in the city's rental registration rules requires it. The city requires the unit to stay registered and inspected at each change in occupancy, so the new owner must keep that registration current for anyone who stays.

faqs.q: How large is the state transfer fee on a typical Millville sale?
faqs.a: At the Census median value of $219,000 the fee comes to $1,083.20 under the state's schedule for sales up to $350,000. The seller pays it when the deed is recorded, and exemptions exist for deeds between spouses or from parent to child.
